message.content: When Copernicus founded his heliocentric theory in the early sixteenth century, Europe was shaped by Renaissance humanism, fragmented monarchies, and the long recovery from papal schism. Poland's elective monarchy and its relatively tolerant legal culture allowed a churchman like Copernicus to serve as canon, diplomat, and economist while protecting his astronomical calculations. At the same time, the Reformation and wars among Habsburg, French, and papal powers made religious authority both fragile and watchful over challenges to received doctrine. His diagram was not cactiform, yet it challenged ecclesiastical authority.
